transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I… I wasn’t sure whether to come in, but what frightened me is I’ve been having thoughts like maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but… it scared me.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, or found that you don’t take pleasure in them anymore?

Yes… I suppose so. I still take out my watercolors sometimes, but I just sit there looking at the paper. The feeling I used to get from the colors… it doesn’t really come, and I end up putting everything away.
Have you been feeling like you’re not worth much, or been blaming yourself for things more than usual?

Yes… I do. I keep thinking about my brother’s decline, going over it again and again. I tell myself if I’d been a better sister, or paid closer attention, maybe I would’ve noticed sooner… maybe prevented some of it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?
Yes… most days, I think. It’s like everything has a gray film over it. Even simple things, making tea or looking at the garden… there’s this heaviness that just sits there.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or fidgety more than usual?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything like that, exactly… maybe I’m just a bit slower getting started, but I couldn’t say if I’m moving or talking differently.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or noticed a decrease in your energy levels most days?
I don’t know… not in a way I’ve really kept track of. I suppose I get worn out, but I couldn’t say it’s most days or anything clear like that.
Have you found it harder to focus on things, like reading or making decisions, more than usual lately?
I’m not sure, really. I haven’t noticed it clearly… I mean, maybe I drift a bit, but I can’t say it’s more than usual.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?
Not really… I haven’t been keeping close track. My appetite seems about the same, I think, and I don’t know that my weight has changed much.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately—like having trouble falling asleep, waking up during the night, or waking up earlier than usual and not being able to go back to sleep?

Yes… somewhat. I don’t always fall asleep easily, and then I wake up around three or four. I start thinking about phone calls or forms, whether I handled things right… and then by morning it feels like I didn’t really rest.
Have you had periods like this before, where you felt down or lost interest in things, or is this the first time you’ve felt this way?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I’ve had low patches before, like anyone, but I don’t know if it was quite like this. I haven’t really thought of it that way.
Looking back, would you say you’ve had other times in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than a couple of weeks?
I’m not sure. I’ve had times where I felt low, yes, but whether it was for more than a couple of weeks or just… life being difficult, I don’t really know.
Looking back on your life, have there been other distinct periods where you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks in a row?

I really don’t know. I can remember being low at different times, but I couldn’t say clearly that it was a separate period like that, for more than two weeks. It’s all a bit hard to sort out looking back.
Looking back, can you recall a specific time when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks at a time?
No… I can’t really point to a specific time like that. I know I’ve felt low here and there, but I don’t remember it clearly enough to say it was more than two weeks.

Looking back on your life, have you ever had a period lasting several weeks where you felt down or lost interest in things to the point it affected your daily life, even if it wasn't as intense as what you're feeling now?

I don’t think I can say for sure. There may have been stretches where I was low and not doing as much, but I don’t really remember it clearly enough to say it was several weeks or that it affected things in a definite way.
Looking back, can you recall a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for several weeks in a row, to the point where it was hard to manage your usual responsibilities or activities?
I’m not really able to remember one clearly. There might have been times I was lower than usual, but I can’t say it went on for several weeks or that it really kept me from managing things.

Looking back, can you recall a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks, and it was followed by a period of at least a couple of months where you felt back to normal or much better?
I’m not sure. I can’t really recall a clear stretch like that, with the timing and then feeling normal again afterward. It’s a bit hard for me to sort out looking back.

Looking back, can you recall a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks, and it was followed by a period of at least a couple of months where you felt back to normal or much better?
I don’t really remember it that clearly. I may have had low periods, but I can’t say there was a definite two-week stretch and then a couple months where I felt normal after.

Looking back, can you recall a time when you felt down or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row, and during that time you also experienced other symptoms like changes in sleep, appetite, energy, or thoughts of worthlessness or death?

Yes… I suppose so. Most days it feels like there’s a kind of gray film over everything. Even simple things, like making tea or looking out at the garden, have this quiet heaviness to them. I can’t really talk myself out of it.

Yes… I think so. It’s like I said, most days there’s this grayness over everything. Even small things, making tea or just looking at the garden, feel heavy somehow. I can’t quite talk myself out of it.
